saints.name: St. John of Matha
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Paris theologian who founded an order to ransom Christians held captive by the Moors…
biography: Born at Faucon in Provence in 1160, John was educated at Aix, lived for a time as a hermit, and went up to Paris, where he took the doctorate in theology and was ordained priest. Tradition relates that at his first Mass he beheld an angel clothed in white, bearing a cross of red and blue, with his hands resting upon two captives, a Christian and a Moor.

To discern the vision he joined the hermit Felix of Valois at Cerfroid, and together they founded the Order of the Most Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives — the Trinitarians — which Innocent III approved in 1198. By their rule a third part of all revenues went to ransom Christians enslaved by the Muslims of Africa and Spain, and the friars were bound, if need be, to give themselves in exchange.

John himself journeyed to spread the order in France, Italy, and Spain, and over the centuries the Trinitarians freed many thousands from bondage. He died at Rome on 17 December 1213, and is invoked as the patron of captives and of the order he founded.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Trinitarian Order for the ransom of captives.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 8 February
